Sources

Crash records: Vermont Agency of Transportation Crash Query Tool, all reported crashes in the Town of Bristol. Reporting agency, address, coordinates, crash type, weather, time of day, impairment and report number are as recorded by VTrans. Five reports in the source export are excluded from this page.

District boundary: parcels carrying Tax Rate #3 in the Town of Bristol Listers' NEMRC grand list export dated September 2 2026, matched by SPAN to the VCGI statewide standardized parcel layer (2025 parcel year) and merged into a single shape. The Police District is the geographic area of the former Village of Bristol, 24 V.S.A. App. ch. 108 § 108-701.

Parcel layer: all 1,630 mapped parcels in Bristol from the same VCGI layer, shaded by whether the Listers' export carries them at Tax Rate #3. Owner names, acreage and SPAN are the public attributes VCGI publishes with that layer.

How the numbers were checked

Every crash with usable coordinates is tested against the district polygon rather than sorted by street name, so a road that crosses the district line is split at the line. 600 of the 691 parcels in the Listers' export have a parcel polygon; the 91 without are mobile home units on leased lots and life-estate units inside a parent parcel already counted, so they do not move the boundary. Interior gaps under five acres were closed. Fifteen detached fringe parcels are kept as separate parts of the district.

All VSP barracks are grouped as Vermont State Police; the barracks name is in each popup. Reports that cannot be plotted have no point to test and are listed above.

Crash data as of August 2026. Boundary as of the September 2 2026 grand list. Page compiled September 9 2026.

This page is written and maintained by Ian Albinson, a member of the Bristol Selectboard, in his own capacity. It is not published by the Town of Bristol, it is not an official Town record, and nothing on it represents a position of the Selectboard, the Listers or the Police Department. The underlying records are public data from the Vermont Agency of Transportation, the Vermont Center for Geographic Information and the Town of Bristol grand list. Errors are mine.
